beliefs: The box splits input on whitespace into words, collapsing runs and stripping leading/trailing whitespace [E2, E3]
Empty or all-whitespace input maps to empty string [E1, E2]
For a single word, the box reverses the whole word, then strips ALL leading 'o' characters from the reversed result [E9, E10, E11, E13]
If stripping leaves the reversed word empty (all o's), the output is 'o' — one 'o' is kept [E9, E11]
For multi-word input, the first word is transformed by the same reverse-then-strip-leading-o rule [E12]
The remaining words are concatenated (no spaces) and reversed as a single chunk [E5, E6, E12]
Multi-word output is transformed-first-word + ' ' + reversed(concatenation of remaining words) [E3, E4, E6, E12]
Case and symbols are preserved within each reversed chunk [E1, E3, E4]
Punctuation attached to a word stays attached and is reversed with the word [E3, E4]
notes: The rule is reverse the whole word then strip leading o's from the reversed result (equivalently strip trailing o's from original then reverse, but keeping the o's that come from interior positions). Fixed predict to reverse first then lstrip('o'), keeping 'o' if empty.
